The polymers were synthesized by free-radical solution addition polymerization from the respective monomers using AIBN as an initiator in THF at $6 0 ~ ^ { \circ } \mathrm { C }$for 48 h. The typical procedure for the synthesis of polymer ia is as follows: The monomer ia (400 mg, 0.67 mol) and AIBN (2 wt %) were dissolved in dry THF (5 mL) and gentle steam ofnitrogen purged into the solution. The solution was kept in an oil bath at $6 0 ~ ^ { \circ } \mathrm { C }$for 48 h. Then, the solution was cooled and poured into excess of methanol to precipitate the product. The crude polymer thus obtained was represipitated twice using chloroform and methanol. The purified polymer was dried at $4 5 ~ ^ { \circ } \mathrm { C }$under vacuum for 48 h to afford yellow colored solid. The remaining Ib–IIc was also prepared by adopting similar procedure as of Ia.

The absorption maximum and shape of the spectra for solution and film were identical for all the polymers (Table 1), ascribed to mesogenic groups did not aggregate in coated film. The representative absorption spectral pattern of polymer Ib and IIb in thin film on quartz substrates are shown in Figure 11. Upon irradiation with UV light, decrease in absorption at 397 nm and 405 nm representing to 2p 2p photocycloaddition of chalcone moiety in thin film of Ib and IIb, respectively. Irradiated polymer films were insoluble in chloroform as well as after irradiation color of film changed from fluorescent yellow to colorless confirmed the photocrosslinking reaction. In addition, the photocrosslinked polymer did not show liquid crystalline property attributed to restricted molecular mobility and attained rigidity by the polymer backbone.
